verdict: P5 is dropped by its own kill criterion: for both presets the paired 95% interval of mean(world - advected) contains zero, and neither preset reaches the 40% reduction (oil is 14% worse, watercolour 19% better within an interval from -19% to +42%). The world anchor does not beat the advected canvas on this orbit. Parity, goldens and cost pass; the art scene, the warp metric, the art module and its runner stay as the stylised track's base.

w1_temporal.prediction_check: I predicted 0.45 to 0.7 for both. Wrong in direction for oil and in size for watercolour.
w1_temporal.why_inferred_not_tested: Inferred, not tested: the anchored canvas compresses the bristle noise (period 1.3 canvas pixels) and the weave (3.2) wherever a surface is foreshortened, above the pixel rate on the grazing ground and the side faces, so pixel centres sliding over the surface sample aliased noise that flickers. The advected canvas keeps its coordinates near one canvas pixel a pixel by construction (it resets where they distort), so it never aliases. Oil, whose bristle noise and impasto relief carry most of the look, loses; watercolour, mostly paper and glaze at lower frequencies, gains but not significantly. A footprint-filtered anchor (fading each noise octave by the chart's derivative) would test this; it is a new proposal, not a revision of P5.

does_not_prove: That world anchoring cannot work: only that this anchor, feeding the painterly shader's unfiltered noise, does not beat the advected canvas on this orbit. GPU time without submission latency (the RHI has no timestamp queries; batching amortises it). Anything about moving objects.
